problem: The caption says the last row is blank and shows the stopping condition, but the figure spec fills that row with the cell '—'; the caption and the drawing disagree. The row labels also say 'length 0/1/2' while the title and the worked example talk about pass numbers, which can make a student think 'length' counts something other than the round.
fix: Either leave the last row truly empty of cells, or say 'the last row shows a dash because no new pair is marked in pass 2'. Label the rows 'pass 0 (strings of length 0)', 'pass 1', 'pass 2 (nothing new)' so the pass number and the string length are clearly the same idea.

problem: The sentence 'Some syllabi describe the inner test as distinguishing one string from another' says nothing usable: the inner test compares two successor states, not two strings. A student will stop and wonder what it means.
fix: Replace it with a plain statement of what the inner test does, for example: 'The inner test asks only whether the two successor states are already known to be distinguishable; the marking then moves one symbol back to (p, q).'

problem: The Myhill-Nerode condition is stated one-sidedly: 'no continuation z makes xz accepted and yz rejected'. As written it does not forbid the reverse case (xz rejected, yz accepted). The phrase 'right-invariant equivalence classes of the Myhill-Nerode relation' is also loose; the relation is a right congruence and its classes are classes of strings.
fix: Write: two strings x and y are equivalent when for every continuation z, xz ∈ L exactly when yz ∈ L (neither order of accept/reject is allowed). Then say the state classes of the minimal DFA correspond one-to-one to these classes of strings.
